_meta.indication: OLUMIANT (baricitinib) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies.
_meta.receipt_date: January 15, 2016 (original NDA, received January 15, 2016 per approval letter); resubmission complete response received December 4, 2017.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study IV (JADW), a confirmatory phase 3 trial
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled 24-week trial; patients received OLUMIANT 2 mg or baricitinib 4 mg once daily or placebo added to background cDMARD treatment, with rescue to baricitinib 4 mg from Week 16 for non-responders.
pivotal_trials.population: 527 patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response or intolerance to 1 or more TNF inhibitor therapies (TNFi-IR).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.n: 527 patients enrolled; primary ACR20 analysis population 176 placebo and 174 OLUMIANT 2 mg.
pivotal_trials.result: Week 12 ACR20 response: OLUMIANT 2 mg 49% vs placebo 27% (treatment difference 22; 95% CI 12, 32).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): upper respiratory tract infections (16.3% with 2 mg vs 11.7% placebo), nausea (2.7% vs 1.6%), herpes simplex, and herpes zoster. Serious risks include serious infections, malignancy, and thrombosis (during the 16-week period venous thromboses occurred in 5 patients on baricitinib 4 mg vs 0 on placebo).
target_moa: Baricitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor; JAKs are intracellular enzymes that transmit cytokine/growth-factor signals and phosphorylate STATs, and baricitinib had greater inhibitory potency at JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 relative to JAK3.
modality: Small molecule (oral JAK inhibitor; molecular weight 371.42).

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MALIGNANCY, AND THROMBOSIS: serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (including tuberculosis and bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections); lymphoma and other malignancies; and thrombosis, including deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism observed at increased incidence versus placebo.

advisory_committee.vote: An Arthritis Advisory Committee was convened on April 23, 2018; it voted 10 Yes, 5 No that the benefit-risk profile was adequate to support approval of baricitinib 2 mg, and 5 Yes, 10 No for the 4 mg dose.

description.text: Added a 1 mg tablet dosage strength for dose adjustment in patients with moderate renal impairment or those taking strong OAT3 inhibitors

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for response to Postmarketing Commitment (PMC 3421-2); Develop a baricitinib 1 mg tablet for dose adjustment in patients with moderate renal impairment or patients taking strong OAT3 inhibitors, noted in the NDA 207924/Original 1, approval letter dated May 31, 2018. description.text: Added new indication for treatment of COVID-19 in hospitalized adults requiring supplemental oxygen, noninvasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or ECMO (with new 4 mg tablet strength)

citations.quote: Olumiant is indicated for the treatment of COVID-19 in hospitalized adults requiring supplemental oxygen, noninvasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

description.text: Added indication for treatment of adult patients with severe alopecia areata

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of the indication for the treatment of adult patients with severe alopecia areata.

summary.text: The original NDA for baricitinib was submitted January 15, 2016 and received a Complete Response action on April 12, 2017 due to unfavorable benefit-risk (venous thrombosis risk); Lilly resubmitted a complete response dated December 4, 2017. An Arthritis Advisory Committee convened on April 23, 2018, and the 2 mg dose was approved with a boxed warning and a required long-term safety postmarketing trial.

citations.quote: The original NDA for baricitinib was submitted on January 14, 2016. Safety concerns were identified, including the risk of venous thrombosis, and the application received a Complete Response (CR) action on April 12, 2017 because the overall benefit-risk assessment of baricitinib 2 mg and 4 mg once daily was not favorable.
We acknowledge receipt of your amendment dated December 4, 2017, which constituted a complete response to our April 12, 2017, action letter.
An Arthritis Advisory Committee (AAC) was convened on April 23, 2018 to discuss this NDA.1 The following is a brief summary of the voting and discussion from the AAC meeting.

requirement.text: PMR 3421-1: Randomized controlled clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety of baricitinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, including two doses of baricitinib and an active comparator, sufficient to evaluate arterial and venous thrombosis, cardiovascular adverse events, opportunistic infections, and malignancy.

citations.quote: 3421-1 Randomized controlled clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety of baricitinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The trial will include two doses of baricitinib and an active comparator. The trial should be of sufficient size and duration to evaluate safety events of interest, including arterial and venous thrombosis, cardiovascular adverse events, opportunistic infections, and malignancy.

requirement.text: PMC 3421-2: Develop a baricitinib 1 mg tablet for dose adjustment in patients with moderate renal impairment or patients taking strong OAT3 inhibitors, and submit the chemistry and manufacturing data to support the 1 mg dosage strength.

citations.quote: 3421-2 Develop a baricitinib 1 mg tablet for dose adjustment in patients with moderate renal impairment or patients taking strong OAT3 inhibitors. Submit the chemistry and manufacturing data to support the 1 mg dosage strength.

On April 12, 2017, a complete response (CR) letter was issued concluding that the overall benefit/risk profile for baricitinib was not favorable given the association of baricitinib with venous thrombotic events (VTE) in the RA clinical program.

basis.text: The overall benefit/risk profile for baricitinib was not favorable given the association of baricitinib with venous thrombotic events (VTE) in the RA clinical program; specific deficiencies included the potential thrombotic risk and inadequate safety exposure for the 2 mg dose.
